questions.question: A vehicle without proper hazmat placards:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper hazmat placards cannot be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: When shipping papers have both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials should be:

options.text: Circled with a pen or marker.
Written the same way as non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: One way to identify hazardous materials on a shipping paper is to highlight them in a contrasting color.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading:

options.text: Does not have to be able to move the vehicle.
Does not need to know about the materials being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person supervising tank loading must stay within 25 feet of the tank, stay alert, see the tank clearly, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The dangers associated with the material.
Where items can be placed on the trailer.
How the material should be loaded and unloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: The dangers associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class describes its dangers.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be kept where the driver can reach them easily while wearing a seat belt, such as in a pouch on the driver's door. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Hazmat shipping papers must include:

options.text: How the materials will be used.

questions.explanation: Drivers must know the dangers of materials they transport. Hazmat shipping papers must include an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: If an explosives package has an oily stain or is damp, the driver should:

options.text: Use towels to absorb the liquid.

questions.explanation: Never transport damaged explosives. Do not accept a package that is damp or has an oily stain.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, the trailer should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle exposed to corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for:
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of hazmat shipping papers for at least two years after the materials are given to the initial carrier. For hazardous waste, the requirement is three years.

questions.question: A Class 7 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: How should small packages that cannot hold a HazMat label be labeled?
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, attach the label to a tag that is secured to the package.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Where can a person stay while watching a parked placarded vehicle?

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person watching a parked placarded vehicle must be awake inside it or within 100 feet of it with a clear view. The person cannot be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: If cargo leaks, how should you identify the hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If you find a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials because this can cause injury or death.

questions.question: When delivering compressed gas, when should you turn off the engine if it runs the pump?
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump during product transfer, turn off the engine before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: Which item is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a fire?

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.
Find someone else to open them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, feel the doors before opening them. If the doors are hot, there may be a fire inside. Keep the doors closed because opening them adds oxygen and makes the fire worse.

questions.question: If a package says "Inhalation Hazard," what placard must be used?
questions.explanation: If a package or shipping paper shows "Inhalation Hazard," use the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: Which does NOT describe someone loading a hazardous materials tank?
questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view, be within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be authorized to move the tank. The required distance is 25 feet, not 10 feet.

questions.question: What must a package with liquid containers display?

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must display arrows pointing in the correct upright direction so the package is placed the right way.

questions.question: How often must employees who work with hazardous materials be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: During loading and unloading, keep the liquid discharge valves open. At all other times, keep them closed.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should NOT be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. You may only park briefly if needed for vehicle operations like refueling. Never park within 5 feet of the road.

questions.question: A person supervising the loading of a tank must:

options.text: Not know the materials being loaded.
Stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the loading of a tank with hazardous materials. This person must be alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should NOT be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Heaters are not permitted when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: You may leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended only:

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may only leave a vehicle with explosives unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations are designed to protect:
questions.explanation: Transporting hazardous materials is risky. Regulations protect you, people around you, and the environment.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be in your vehicle?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, you must have an approved gas mask in your vehicle.

questions.question: Which type of material may require a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials require a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. The total transport index of all cargo in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: The only proper way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: Check each tire on your vehicle at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only accurate way to check tire pressure.
